gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Heavy, bendy lettering: Plakkaat curls its terminals nearly back to the stem, while Noto Sans Old Persian stands tall. Plakkaat is built to punch, while the body font is built to breathe.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-old-tur: Chunky bent-wire capitals, heavy and nearly closed at every curl. Let Plakkaat go big and let Noto Sans Old Turkic, chunky, tall and open-mouthed, sit a few steps smaller.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Plakkaat is all closed, heavy curls, terminals swinging round to nearly meet the stem. Noto Sans Oriya opens every curve wide, and that closed-versus-open split is what makes the pairing work.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Bent-straw strokes, heavy and uniform, make Plakkaat look drawn with a single pen tip. And Noto Sans Osmanya counters with oversized lowercase and wide, easy s turns that loosen everything up.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-: Wire-bent and weighty: the s curves in Plakkaat never thin at the spine, while Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong sits high and open. One hits hard, the other carries text quietly.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-phoenic: Heavy, closed, bent-wire capitals on top, terminals curling almost home. Noto Sans Phoenician sits beneath, its s curves open at both ends, so the two lean on each other.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-psalter: Heavy, rounded and loud, Plakkaat curls its terminals almost back into the stem. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, with gaping e mouths and low-rising capitals, reads best a few sizes down.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Heavy and tightly closed, Plakkaat bends its lines like straw, while Noto Sans Rejang opens wide, porthole-style counters. Its open gaps in the a and s stay distinct line after line.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-runic: Heavy lettering that curls shut at the edges leads, and Noto Sans Runic, with curves that never close on themselves, takes over. One slams the door, the other leaves it ajar.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Heavy, bent-straw lettering whose curls nearly close back on the stem. Plakkaat is best at loud, solid statements, while Noto Sans Siddham is best at quiet openness, its s ends hanging far from the spine.
